page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The server features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 524 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2707.99, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 43272.98 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14393.0. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with a PassMark memory score of 2782.36 in the top 25%, though uncached large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes remain in the average tier at 73.78 GB/sec and 39.88 GB/sec respectively. Image processing benchmarks also show strong performance at 14298.0.

For workloads, the E32as_v4 is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and text processing. It handles Redis SET operations at an average rate of 31.48 million operations per second. While it demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small 135M LLM models at 310.9 tokens/sec, its performance drops significantly for larger models, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 25% at 6.62 tokens/sec. This highlights a clear tradeoff: while highly efficient for memory-heavy databases and standard enterprise applications, it is not optimized for large-scale LLM inference.
